output.answer_markdown: Yes. The filings describe ongoing matters tied to each year. For 2022, a federal court in Ohio issued a $651 million judgment against three defendants, including the Company, which the Company is appealing [1]. The Company also agreed in principle to a national opioid settlement with a maximum payable of about $4.3 billion in remediation [2], and settled Florida opioid claims for $484 million in March 2022 [3]. The Delaware Attorney General moved for partial intervention in the Gill qui tam case in July 2022 [5]. For 2021, the consolidated ERISA case was dismissed without prejudice in October 2021 [6], and the Company received a books-and-records demand in December 2021 [7]. For 2020, the DOJ served a DEA administrative subpoena in January 2020 concerning opioid and controlled substance practices [4].
